title: Lipidomics Analysis Protocol
author: Oliver Fiehn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ys7fwhn
materials: Preparation of solutions a. Preparation of Tuning Solution • 88.5 mL acetonitrile • 1.5 mL H ² O • 10 mL Agilent Low Concentration ESI Tuning Mix • 5 µL 322 Reference Ion (sonicate before use) • Degas by sonication for 5 min • 100 mL will typically last months b. Preparation of Reference Mass Solution • 95 mL acetonitrile • 5 mL H ² O • 100 µL 5 mM 921 Reference Ion (sonicate before use) • 125 µL 5 mM TFA Reference Ion (sonicate before use) • 125 µL 10 mM Purine Reference Ion (sonicate before use) • Degas by sonication for 5 min c. Mobile phase A (60:40 ACN:water + 10 mM Ammonium Formate + 0.1% Formic Acid) (1). Pre-rinse three times 1 L glass bottle with pure acetonitrile (2). Measure exactly 600 mL of acetonitrile in a pre-rinsed graduated cylinder and add them to the 1 L glass bottle. (3). Measure exactly 400 mL of MilliQ water in a pre-rinsed graduated cylinder and add them to the 1 L glass bottle. (4). Add 1 mL formic acid (5). Weight 0.630 g of ammonium formate and add them to the glass bottle (6). Sonicate for 10 min at room temperature until all the ammonium formate is dissolved. (7). 1 L will last for around 200 samples d. Mobile phase B (90:10 IPA:ACN + 10 mM Ammonium Formate + 0.1% Formic Acid) (1). Measure exactly 100 mL of acetonitrile in a pre-rinsed graduated cylinder and add them to the 1 L glass bottle. (2). Add 1 mL formic acid (3). Weight 0.630 g of ammonium formate and add them to the glass bottle (4). Sonicate for 40 min at 70ºC until all the ammonium formate is dissolved. (5). 1 L will last for around 200 samples

steps.title: Perform Instrument Tuning
steps.instruction: Tune the instrument before each run of 300 sample batch using a freshly prepared Tuning Solution in Tune mode.

substeps.instruction: Perform a 'Standard Tune' and print the tune report.
In ESI(+), verify calibrant profile and ensure ion intensities are: m/z 322.0481 > 400k, m/z 622.0290 > 200k, and m/z 922.0098 > 200k.
In ESI(–), verify calibrant profile and ensure ion intensities are: m/z 301.9981 > 800k, m/z 601.9790 > 800k, and m/z 1033.9881 > 1100k.
If any ion intensity is below these values, clean the ion source and repeat the tuning.

steps.title: Check Reference Ions
steps.instruction: Verify lock mass using a freshly prepared Reference Ion Mass Solution in Acquisition mode.

substeps.instruction: Pump the reference mass solution at 0.150 mL/min, split 1:10 before entering the mass spectrometer.
In ESI(+), check that m/z 121.0509 is 40–60k and m/z 922.0098 is 8–12k; adjust recipe and flow rates if necessary.
In ESI(–), check that m/z 112.9856 is 10–20k and m/z 966.0007 is 10–20k; adjust recipe and flow rates if necessary.

steps.title: Install New Column
steps.instruction: Install and condition a new UPLC column coupled to a VanGuard pre-column.

substeps.instruction: Purge the pumping system of buffer-containing mobile phases and connect the column inlet to the injector outlet.
Flush the column with 100% acetonitrile: start at 0.1 mL/min and increase to 0.6 mL/min over 5 min.
Stop flow and attach the column outlet to the mass spectrometer ion source.
Gradually increase flow with 100% acetonitrile from 0.1 mL/min to 0.6 mL/min over 5 min and monitor for steady backpressure.
Stop flow and flush with mobile phase (A) and (B) at a 50:50 ratio: start at 0.1 mL/min and increase to 0.6 mL/min over 5 min.
Monitor backpressure; for a new column, it should be 500–550 bar at the start of injection (elution at 40% mobile phase B).
Inject 5 methanol blanks and record the lowest and highest backpressure values for the first and last samples.
Inject 10 citrate plasma samples and record the lowest and highest backpressure values for the first and last samples.

steps.title: Execute Pre-run Sequence
steps.instruction: Run a validation sequence before starting the main analysis to ensure system performance.

substeps.instruction: Inject the following sequence: 1x 'No sample injection', 5x Blank (methanol), 2x QC-mix, and 2x Citrate plasma.
Using MassHunter Qualitative Analysis software, monitor the QC-mix for retention time, intensity, S/N, mass accuracy, and peak width (FWHM) against default values in TEDDY_QC-mix_default.XLS.
If retention time shift >±2.5% or FWHM increases >20%, replace the VanGuard pre-column and/or UPLC column.
If intensity of particular analytes is <10 ppm, clean the ion source.
Compare the citrate plasma TIC intensity to a previous sequence; variation must be <±15%.
Verify backpressure: 500–580 bar at start (40% B) and 850–1000 bar at 99% B. If initial backpressure is 580–725 bar, replace the VanGuard pre-column; if still high, replace the UPLC column.

steps.title: Select Lipid Analysis Method
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate method from the system folder based on the required ion mode.

substeps.instruction: Positive ion mode: TEDDY_CSHC18_100mm_POS_MS_mode
Negative ion mode: TEDDY_CSHC18_100mm_NEG_MS_mode
Positive ion MSMS mode: TEDDY_CSHC18_100mm_POS_MSMS_mode
Negative ion MSMS mode: TEDDY_CSHC18_100mm_NEG_MSMS_mode

steps.title: Store Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the column for storage to avoid precipitation of mobile-phase buffers.

substeps.instruction: Flush column with 50% acetonitrile: start at 0.1 mL/min, increase to 0.6 mL/min over 5 min, and maintain for 10 min.
Flush column with 100% acetonitrile: start at 0.1 mL/min, increase to 0.6 mL/min over 5 min, and maintain for 10 min.
Remove the column from the system and store in the box.
